item.title: Day 1
item.description:
Temas del Día #

  • Magic Questions and Phrases**
  • Greetings**
  • Definite and Infinite Articles**

Objetivos del aprendizaje #

Al finalizar esta clase, serás capaz de: #

1. Utilizar exclusivamente el idioma inglés en el salón de clases mediante el uso constante de frases y preguntas básicas/comunes.

item.title: Day 1
item.description:
Temas del Día #

Simple Present Rules and Uses 3rd Person Singular Rule Simple Present Time Expressions

Objetivos del aprendizaje: #

Al finalizar esta clase, serás capaz de: #

1. Identificar y utilizar el presente simple para describir hábitos, tradiciones y verdades generales en oraciones afirmativas y negativas, en preparación para hablar de ti mismo en entrevistas de trabajo y proporcionar información importante a tus clientes.

item.title: Day 1
item.description:
Topics of the day #

  • Simple Past Rules and Uses
  • Verbs in Simple Past
  • Regular verbs pronunciation

Learning Objectives: #

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Describe past actions or interactions by using affirmative and negative sentences in the simple past.
  2. Use common simple past verbs to explain completed actions during customer service calls (Example: processed requests, handled complaints, updated accounts).
  3. Accurately pronounce regular past tense verb endings (-ed) to ensure clear and professional communication over the phone.

Introduction: #

Today, you will learn how to talk about past situations in a call center. You will practice how to form sentences to describe what happened during a call, including things you did and things you didn’t do. You will also learn common action words in their past form to explain tasks like helping customers, solving problems, and updating information. Finally, you will practice how to pronounce regular verb endings correctly, so your speech is clear and professional when speaking with customers. Important terms (Vocabulary):

item.title: Day 1
item.description:
Topics of the Day: #

  • Simple Future
  • Time Expressions
  • Prepositions of Time (Review)

Learning Objectives: #

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Use the simple future tense in affirmative, negative, and question forms to talk about plans, predictions, and decisions.
  2. Identify and use common time expressions for the future (e.g., tomorrow, next week, later) to give more detail about when actions will happen, in preparation for the call center experience.
  3. Apply prepositions of time (in, on, at) correctly when talking about future events and schedules.

Introduction: #

Today you will learn how to talk about things that haven’t happened yet by forming sentences in different ways, including statements, negatives, and questions. You will also practice adding details about when something will happen using common future time phrases, and review how to choose the correct time prepositions to make your ideas clear and accurate.

item.title: Day 1 - Week 1
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Pronounce and spell the English alphabet correctly.
  • ✅ Recognize and say numbers from 0 to 1,000,000 including teen/ten differences and TH sounds.
  • ✅ Use titles like Mr., Mrs., Ms. properly.
  • ✅ Apply basic connected speech rules for natural pronunciation.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will pronounce and spell words correctly following the Alphabet and the Military Phonetic Alphabet. Besides, you will recognize and write numbers from 1 to 1,000,000. You will be able to understand the differences of teen/ten and practice the TH sound. Finally, you will learn how to use titles properly and address people in a polite manner. You will also learn two basic rules of connected speech.

item.title: Day 1 - Week 2
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Review class rules, magic questions, and Simple Present tense thoroughly.
  • ✅ Learn regular vs. irregular Simple Past verbs.
  • ✅ Focus on ED ending pronunciation and memorize 80 common verbs for storytelling and past events.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will reinforce Week 1 foundations while introducing Simple Past verbs. As A1 students, you must follow the class rules and use the magic questions for English-only participation. Finally, you will memorize past tense verbs to describe yesterday’s actions or experiences.

item.title: Day 1 - Week 3
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Use the simple future with “will” to make predictions, decisions, and promises.
  • ✅ Use “be going to” to talk about plans and intentions.
  • ✅ Identify and use common future signal words (tomorrow, next week, soon).
  • ✅ Recognize and use basic future clauses in sentences (when, if, before, after).

📖 Introduction #

Today you will review key future forms, including “will”, “be going to”, future signal words, and basic future clauses. You will practice how to talk about plans, predictions, and decisions in real-life situations. As an A1 student, mastering these structures will help you communicate about future events in contexts such as scheduling, making arrangements, and basic workplace interactions.

item.title: Day 1 - Week 4
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Compare different people, animals, things, or places using comparative adjectives.
  • ✅ Explain the difference between two nouns using the correct comparative form.
  • ✅ Express equality between two nouns using as + adjective + as.
  • ✅ Highlight one outstanding noun from a group using superlative adjectives.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will learn how to use comparative and superlative adjectives to compare people, animals, things, or places that are different — and to express when they are the same. You will also learn how to describe one outstanding noun that stands out from a group. These structures are essential for everyday conversations, descriptions, and professional communication.

item.title: Day 2
item.description:
Topics of the Day: #

  • Frequency adverbs
  • Daily Routine
  • Hobbies
  • Simple Present Interrogative Structure

Learning Objectives: #

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Describe your daily routine and habits using frequency adverbs and expressions (e.g., always, usually, sometimes), to get ready to explain during a job interview how you manage responsibilities.
  2. Talk about your hobbies and interests to build rapport with interviewers and participate in small talk in a professional setting.
  3. Ask and answer questions about your routine and hobbies, as well as how often activities occur.

Introduction: #

Today, you will learn how to talk about your daily routine, hobbies, and traditions, and how to use frequency adverbs and expressions such as always, usually, sometimes, and never to describe how often you do things. This will help you talk about your habits and personal activities clearly.

item.title: Day 2
item.description:
Temas del día #

  • How to pray in English: FOR vs. TO
  • The Alphabet
  • Verb

Objetivos del aprendizaje: #

Al finalizar esta clase, serás capaz de:

  1. Orar al iniciar cada clase, utilizando FOR + Sustantivos para agradecer, y TO + Verbos para pedir.
  2. Pronunciar el abecedario con los nombres correctos de cada letra, para deletrear tu propio nombre, nombres de tus clientes, nombres de ciudades, y otras palabras importantes en el idioma inglés.
  3. Utilizar el alfabeto militar para que tus futuros clientes puedan reconocer una letra con facilidad a través de una llamada telefónica.
  4. Nombrar acciones que realizas tú u otras personas, reconociendo los verbos más comunes en el idioma inglés y pronunciándolos correctamente.

Introducción: #

El día de hoy, fortalecerás tres bases fundamentales para tu desarrollo en el idioma inglés. A través del vocabulario para orar, aprenderás a utilizar de forma básica “for” y “to”, evitando uno de los errores más comunes en niveles básicos ya que, aunque parecen similares, son usadas en contextos completamente diferentes. Dominar estas preposiciones te permitirá comunicar ideas con mayor precisión y claridad en contextos cotidianos.

item.title: Day 2
item.description:
Topics of the day #

  • Verb Be in Past
  • Time Expressions (Simple Past)
  • Questions Words (Review)
  • Simple Past Question Structures

Learning Objectives: #

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Use the past of the verb be (was/were) with time expressions to describe past customer issues and interactions clearly.
  2. Ask and answer questions using Wh- question words in correct simple past question structures.

Introduction: #

Today, you will learn how to talk about past experiences or states using the verb “be”. This includes describing events and interactions, asking questions to understand past issues, and giving clear information about previous situations. We will focus on using the past of the verb be (was/were), simple past verbs with time expressions, and forming questions using Wh- words and correct structures. These skills will help you communicate more effectively, ask better questions, and get ready to use them in a call center environment. By the end of the lesson, you’ll be able to confidently talk about past events and handle customer conversations related to previous issues.

item.title: Day 2
item.description:
Topics of the Day: #

  • Demonstrative adjectives
  • There is vs. There are
  • Singulars and Plurals

Learning Objectives: #

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Use demonstrative adjectives (this, that, these, those) to identify and describe objects based on distance.
  2. Use there is and there are correctly to talk about the existence of singular and plural nouns.
  3. Identify singular and plural nouns, and use them correctly in simple sentences. You will also be able to use irregular plurals correctly and avoid common beginner mistakes regarding plurals.

Introduction: #

Today you will build essential language skills to describe things clearly and accurately, especially in situations like assisting customers over the phone. First, you will learn how to point out and describe items depending on how near or far they are from you or the caller, which is very useful when giving or confirming information about objects. Next, you will practice how to mention whether something exists or is available, using the correct structure for one item or multiple items. This will help you communicate details about products, services, or locations more effectively. Finally, you will work on recognizing the difference between one item and more than one, forming plural nouns correctly, including some special cases, and avoiding common mistakes. This will support you when giving clear and accurate information to customers.

item.title: Day 2 - Week 1
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Master Simple Present with “to be” (am/is/are) and other verbs for descriptions, habits, and routines — in affirmative, negative, and question forms.
  • ✅ Use “to be” + adjectives correctly to describe people and things.
  • ✅ Apply possessive adjectives to show ownership properly.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will describe people and things using adjectives and the verb “to be” correctly. You will talk about daily habits and truths with other verbs. Finally, you will show ownership using possessives for real-life conversations like work or family talk.

item.title: Day 2 - Week 2
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Use Simple Past with “to be” (was/were) in affirmative, negative, and question forms.
  • ✅ Use Simple Past with other verbs (regular & irregular) for completed actions — affirmative, negative, interrogative, and short answers.
  • ✅ Focus on pronunciation and use past tense for storytelling and past events.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will use the Simple Past tense to talk about finished actions — “I went yesterday.” As A1 students, use it for recapping weekend plans or sharing life experiences beyond present routines.

item.title: Day 2 - Week 3
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Use the present continuous to describe actions happening now.
  • ✅ Use the present continuous to talk about future arrangements.
  • ✅ Identify time expressions related to present and future (now, right now, tonight, tomorrow).
  • ✅ Describe personal plans and scheduled activities using appropriate structure and vocabulary.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will learn and practice the present continuous for actions happening now and for future arrangements. You will focus on how to describe current activities and talk about planned events in real-life situations. As an A1 student, mastering these structures will help you communicate effectively in contexts such as scheduling, making plans, and basic workplace or customer service interactions.

item.title: Day 2 - Week 4
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Use gerunds and infinitives correctly according to each rule.
  • ✅ Identify and explain the difference between gerunds and infinitives.
  • ✅ Recognize the 4 verbs that change in meaning depending on whether a gerund or infinitive follows.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will learn the difference between a gerund (verb + -ing) and an infinitive (to + verb). You will explore the different rules for when to use each one, and discover 4 special verbs that change their meaning depending on which form follows them.

item.title: Day 3
item.description:
Temas del día: #

  • Personal Pronouns
  • Verb to “be”
  • Professions
  • Expressing feelings
  • Contries and Nationalities
  • Introduce Yourself

Objetivos del aprendizaje: #

Al finalizar esta clase, serás capaz de:

  1. Identificar y utilizar correctamente los pronombres personales para referirte a ti mismo y a otras personas en oraciones simples.
  2. Utilizar correctamente el Verbo “Be” (Ser o Estar) para formar oraciones básicas que describan identidad, origen y otras características personales.
  3. Saber y recordar vocabulario básico sobre profesiones, sentimientos, países y nacionalidades para poder presentarte a ti mismo y a otras personas con información personal básica en conversaciones simples. (Preparación para entrevistas laborales)

Introducción: #

El día de hoy aprenderás a utilizar los pronombres personales y las diferentes formas del verbo “be”, dos elementos fundamentales para formar oraciones básicas en inglés y hablar sobre ti mismo y otras personas.

item.title: Day 3
item.description:
Topics of the Day:

  • The weather & Temperature
  • Days of the week
  • Ordinal numbers
  • Months of the Year
  • How to read year
  • Dates

Learning Objectives:

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Identify and communicate dates and schedules clearly by using days of the week, months, ordinal numbers, and years.
  2. Describe and understand weather conditions and temperatures in order to respond to customer inquiries related to deliveries, or service interruptions caused by weather.
  3. Accurately read and state dates and years when verifying customer information, explaining billing periods, or scheduling future services.

Introduction: #

Today you will learn how to talk about time, dates, and weather in English, which are important skills for call center agents. You will practice using days of the week, months, ordinal numbers, and years to correctly say and confirm dates with customers.

item.title: Day 3
item.description:
Topics of the Day: #

  • Parts of an Address
  • US States and Abbreviations
  • How to ask for an address

Learning Objectives: #

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Identify and correctly organize the parts of a U.S. address (street number, street name, city, state, ZIP code) when listening to or reading customer information.
  2. Recognize and match common U.S. states with their abbreviations (e.g., CA = California, NY = New York) to prepare for customer interactions.
  3. Confirm and repeat an address clearly using appropriate call center language (e.g., “Let me verify that for you…”).
  4. Ask follow-up questions to clarify missing or unclear information (e.g., “Could you repeat the ZIP code?” or “Is that Avenue or Street?”).

Introduction: #

Today, you will learn about the different parts of an address in the United States and how they are organized, which is a topic of great importance for your certification and also for your goal to get a job in the call center industry. You will also learn the names of U.S. states and their abbreviations, which are commonly used in customer information, please memorize these abbreviations, they will be extremely helpful in the future. In addition, you will practice how to ask for an address in a polite and professional way during a call. These skills will help you handle customer information more clearly and confidently.

item.title: Day 3
item.description:
Day 3 – Week 4 #

Topics of the Day: #

  • Parts of the body
  • Punctuation and Intonation

Learning Objectives: #

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Identify and correctly use basic parts of the body vocabulary in spoken and written English, which would be useful in interpretation settings such as medical call centers.
  2. Recognize and apply basic punctuation marks (periods, commas, question marks, etc.) to improve clarity and meaning when reading aloud.
  3. Use appropriate intonation patterns (rising and falling tone) when reading sentences aloud to convey meaning, emotions, and sentence type (questions, statements, etc.).

Introduction: #

Today, you will learn how to name and describe different areas of the human body so you can communicate clearly in real-life situations, including professional environments like healthcare support or interpretation calls. You will also explore how punctuation marks help organize ideas in a text and guide you to read more clearly and naturally. Finally, you will practice using your voice effectively by applying the correct tone when reading, helping you express meaning, ask questions, and sound more natural in English.

item.title: Day 3 - Week 1
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Form Simple Present 3rd person singular sentences and apply spelling rules correctly (+s / +es / +ies).
  • ✅ Use subject, object, and reflexive pronouns correctly.
  • ✅ Use frequency adverbs (always, sometimes, rarely…) and daily routine vocabulary to describe habits and answer “How often…?” questions fluently.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will learn the 3rd person Simple Present rules with pronouns and nouns for talking about other people’s actions and routines — “She always wakes herself up” — for work schedules, family habits, or daily life conversations. Finally, you will use indefinite and definite frequency adverbs to say how often things happen.

item.title: Day 3 - Week 2
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Use possessive adjectives to indicate belonging or ownership to a person, animal, or thing.
  • ✅ Use possessive pronouns to replace a possessive adjective + noun and avoid repetition.
  • ✅ Form a possessive noun by adding ’s (or ’) to show ownership.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will use possessive adjectives, pronouns, and nouns to show ownership or a close relationship to someone or something.

item.title: Day 3 - Week 3
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Identify and use singular and plural nouns correctly.
  • ✅ Differentiate between count and non-count nouns.
  • ✅ Use common quantifiers (some, any, much, many, a lot of) appropriately.
  • ✅ Apply these structures in everyday contexts such as shopping, describing quantities, and basic workplace communication.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will learn and practice singular and plural nouns, count and non-count nouns, and common quantifiers. You will focus on how to describe quantities and talk about everyday items in real-life situations. As an A1 student, mastering these structures will help you communicate effectively in contexts such as shopping, ordering food, describing items, and basic workplace or customer service interactions.

item.title: Day 3 - Week 4
item.description:
📖 Introduction #

This is a practice material to help you study and get ready for your certification test. Here, you will find all the topics you learned throughout the month with your teachers. This material includes exercises in preparation for your certification test, make sure to be conscious and practice everything you can in order to feel prepared for your test. Don’t forget to be honest when you do the exercises included.

item.title: Day 4
item.description:
Temas del día #

  • Cardinal Numbers
  • The time
  • Money Vocabulary

Objetivos del aprendizaje: #

Al finalizar esta clase, serás capaz de:

  1. Decir y entender los números cardinales de 1 a 100 en inglés, para compartir información como números de teléfono, cantidades o direcciones con un cliente.
  2. Preguntar y decir la hora en inglés para informar a un cliente sobre horarios de atención, tiempos de servicio, e historial de transacciones.
  3. Usar vocabulario básico de dinero en inglés para hablar de precios, pagos y costos.

Introducción: #

El día de hoy desarrollarás las bases para comprender y comunicar información numérica en inglés, aprendiendo a decir y comprender los números del 1 al 100, algo fundamental al interactuar con clientes.

item.title: Day 4
item.description:
Topics of the Day:

  • Prepositions of Time
  • Adjectives (Including Colors)
  • Possessive Adjectives
  • Family Members

Learning Objectives: #

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Identify and correctly use prepositions of time (in, on, at) to talk about schedules, dates, and daily activities.
  2. Use adjectives, including colors, to describe people, objects, and places, in preparation for the certification test and job interviews.
  3. Use possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, our, their) to show possession or relationship in different sentences.
  4. Identify and describe family members using basic vocabulary.

Introduction: #

Today you will learn how to talk about time, describe people and things, show possession, and speak about family members in English. First, you will practice using prepositions of time such as in, on, and at to talk about dates, days, and parts of the day. Then, you will learn how to use adjectives, including colors, to describe people, objects, and places in simple sentences.

item.title: Day 4
item.description:
Topics of the Day: #

  • Food Vocabulary
  • Animals
  • Clothes
  • Parts of the House

Learning Objectives: #

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Use basic food vocabulary to ask and answer simple questions.
  2. Recognize and name common animals in visual and audio prompts.
  3. Use clothing vocabulary to describe what someone is wearing in simple sentences, and to describe your own outfit as well.
  4. Use basic vocabulary to describe locations within a house (e.g., kitchen, bedroom) in simple sentences.

Introduction: #

Today you will learn how to talk about everyday topics using simple English. We will practice how to communicate about things we see and use in our daily lives, like meals, animals, outfits, and places at home. First, you will explore words related to different kinds of food and practice how to use them in basic conversations. Then, you will learn how to identify different animals through images and listening activities. After that, you will focus on clothing and how to talk about what people are wearing, including how to describe your own outfits. Finally, we will learn how to talk about different areas inside a home and explain where things are. By the end of the lesson, you will feel more confident understanding and using common vocabulary in simple, clear sentences.

item.title: Day 4
item.description:
Day 4 – Week 4 #

Topics of the Day: #

  • A1 Self-Study Practice Guide (Certification Prep)

Learning Objectives: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Produce simple spoken sentences to talk about personal information, descriptions, daily routines, past activities, and free time using basic vocabulary and structures.
  2. Demonstrate basic pronunciation skills by clearly spelling words, reading numbers and dates, and pronouncing common words and endings (e.g., -s, -ed).
  3. Read short sentences and simple information aloud with understandable pronunciation, appropriate pauses, and correct expansion of abbreviations (e.g., addresses).

Introduction: #

Welcome to your pre-certification day. Today’s focus is to help you get ready for your certification interview and written test. The exercises below are designed to help you review and expand your vocabulary so that you can answer the questions clearly and confidently. Please work on this guide carefully and thoughtfully. The more effort you put into building your answers correctly, the better prepared you will be for your certification. Follow the instructions in this guide as they are. If it asks you to say or read something aloud, please do it, even if you are alone. Practicing out loud will help build your confidence. This guide is designed for independent work, as you should already have the knowledge to complete it on your own and even notice some of your mistakes. However, you can always ask your teacher for guidance if you have questions about any section. Take advantage of this time to prepare, and enjoy!

item.title: Day 4 - Week 1
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Read and say time in American English (“Ten o-three”, “Twelve o’clock”).
  • ✅ Reinforce daily routine vocabulary and frequency adverbs from Day 3.
  • ✅ Learn American mailing address format and state abbreviations.
  • ✅ Practice giving professional opinions, agreements, and disagreements for call center skills.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will review all the topics from the week — routines, frequency adverbs, 3rd person rule, and pronouns — while adding practical skills: time-telling, addresses, and opinion phrases. As an A1 student, you must master these for work schedules, directions, customer service, or daily planning conversations.

item.title: Day 4 - Week 2
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Learn the different prepositions of time and know when to use them.
  • ✅ Use the different prepositions of place.
  • ✅ Use demonstrative adjectives to point and refer to objects.
  • ✅ Learn new vocabulary about navigating online.
  • ✅ Describe the way of doing something using adverbs of manner.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will learn new vocabulary about technology. At the end of the class, you will know how to use prepositions of time and place. You will also know how to refer to objects that are near or far from you. Finally, you will be able to describe how something is done.

item.title: Day 4 - Week 3
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Use can to talk about ability, permission, possibility, and making requests in the present.
  • ✅ Use could to talk about past ability, permission, possibility, and making polite requests.
  • ✅ Differentiate between can and could in questions, statements, and negative forms.
  • ✅ Apply can and could in real-life situations such as making requests, giving permission, describing abilities, or politely asking for help.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will learn and practice can and could to talk about ability, permission, possibility, and requests. You will focus on how to describe what you or others are able to do, ask for help politely, and give or deny permission in real-life situations. As an A1 student, mastering these structures will help you communicate effectively in contexts such as work, school, customer service, or daily conversations.

item.title: Day 4 - Week 4
item.description:
🎯 Learning Objectives #

At the end of the class, you will be able to:

  • ✅ Give instructions explaining complete procedures using sequence words.
  • ✅ Give commands, orders, or tell people what to do or what they need to do.

📖 Introduction #

Today you will learn how to explain procedures you have to follow in order to do something. You will also be able to use words and use the correct structure of sentences to give orders, commands, or tell other people what to do.
